_comment: ISO 14064 — the other way to account for the same emissions.
ISO 14064-1:2018 dropped the three-scope model for six categories, and the
difference is not cosmetic: it splits GHG Protocol's Scope 3 across four
categories on a different principle, and it requires an organisation to
assess the significance of every indirect category and justify anything left
out. A company certified to ISO 14064-1 and reporting under the GHG Protocol
is presenting one inventory two ways, and should not be recomputing it.
The mapping below is what lets this tool present the same numbers either way.
iso.org could not be reached from the build environment, so the category
definitions and the mapping come from practitioner and certifier summaries
and are graded medium. Where sources disagreed the disagreement is recorded
on the mapping rather than resolved silently.

sources.title: ISO 14064-1:2018 — Specification with guidance at the organization level
ISO 14064-3:2019 — Verification and validation of greenhouse gas statements
GHG Protocol vs ISO 14064-1: alignment and when to use each
ISO 14064 and GHG Protocol carbon mapping guide

categories.name: Direct GHG emissions and removals
categories.note: Emissions from sources owned or controlled by the organisation. Directly equivalent to Scope 1.

categories.name: Indirect GHG emissions from imported energy
categories.note: Generation of imported electricity, heat, steam and cooling. Directly equivalent to Scope 2.

categories.name: Indirect GHG emissions from transportation
categories.note: Upstream and downstream transport and distribution, business travel, employee commuting and customer transport — which the GHG Protocol splits across four separate Scope 3 categories.

categories.name: Indirect GHG emissions from products used by the organization
categories.note: Purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy related activities, waste generated in operations, and upstream leased assets.

categories.name: Indirect GHG emissions associated with the use of products from the organization
categories.note: Processing and use of sold products, end-of-life treatment, downstream leased assets, franchises and investments.

categories.name: Indirect GHG emissions from other sources
categories.note: Anything material that categories 2 to 5 do not cover. Deliberately open, and correspondingly rare in practice.

significance.note: ISO 14064-1:2018 strengthened the treatment of indirect emissions: an organisation must assess the significance of every indirect category and document its justification for any category excluded from the inventory. That is a stronger obligation than the GHG Protocol's optional Scope 3 — under ISO you must consider all of it and say why anything is out.

part3.note: Requirements for validating and verifying GHG statements — selecting the verifier, agreeing the level of assurance, and setting objectives, criteria and scope.

levels.name: Limited assurance
levels.note: A negative-form conclusion: nothing came to the verifier's attention suggesting the statement is materially misstated.

levels.name: Reasonable assurance
levels.note: A positive-form conclusion, with more extensive procedures. Materiality is commonly set at 5% for reasonable assurance, which drives the nature, timing and extent of the work.

other_parts.note: Project-level quantification, monitoring and reporting of emission reductions or removal enhancements. Applies to a mitigation project, not a corporate inventory.
Carbon footprint of products — quantification at product rather than organisation level. Out of scope for this tool.
Guidance on applying ISO 14064-1, published 2025. This tool does not implement it.

line_mapping.note: Direct emissions from owned or controlled sources.
Purchased goods and services — a product used by the organisation.

Waste generated in operations. Most mappings place waste disposal in category 4 as a service purchased by the organisation; at least one secondary source places organisation-produced waste in category 6 instead. Category 4 is used here and the disagreement is recorded rather than hidden.
Use of sold products — a product from the organisation.
Investments — downstream, grouped with use of products from the organisation.

differences.ghgp: Scope 3 is optional under the Corporate Standard
differences.iso: Every indirect category must be assessed for significance, and exclusions justified
differences.why_it_matters: An inventory that satisfies the GHG Protocol by omitting Scope 3 does not satisfy ISO 14064-1.

differences.ghgp: Three scopes, with fifteen Scope 3 categories
differences.iso: Six categories, splitting indirect emissions on a different principle
differences.why_it_matters: The totals reconcile exactly; the presentation does not. Reporting both means presenting one inventory two ways, not computing it twice.

differences.ghgp: Removals handled separately from the inventory
differences.iso: Direct removals sit inside category 1 alongside direct emissions
differences.why_it_matters: A company with material removals will show a different category 1 than its Scope 1.

differences.ghgp: No verification standard of its own
differences.iso: ISO 14064-3 specifies how validation and verification are conducted
differences.why_it_matters: A GHG Protocol inventory is commonly verified against ISO 14064-3 or ISAE 3410 — the accounting standard and the assurance standard are separate choices.
